transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

I’m here because my sleep has gotten really bad. I lie awake going over client models in my head, and then I’ll wake up around three or four with my stomach all tight. By the time I go to work, it feels like I haven’t rested at all.
How long has this pattern of lying awake worrying and waking up at 3 or 4 a.m. been going on?
About three years now—since the merger reorganized our Caribbean-market division.

Besides worrying about work at night, do you find yourself excessively worrying about other things in your life—like health, finances, or family—during the day, and having trouble controlling that worry?
I’m not really sure. It’s mostly work that keeps circling in my head.
Over the past few weeks, have you noticed feeling down, depressed, or losing interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy?

Yes. Most days I feel this heavy, gray kind of sadness, at work and even at home. I’m just going through the motions, and sometimes I have to try not to cry if someone asks me something completely normal.
How many weeks or months has this low, sad mood and loss of interest in things been going on?
About three years, I think. It started around the time of that merger and the reorganization of our Caribbean-market division.
Over these past three years, has there ever been a stretch of two months or longer when you felt essentially back to your normal self, without the sadness or low mood?
No, I don’t think so. It’s been there pretty much continuously since the merger and the Caribbean division reorganization, about three years now.
Besides the low mood, have you noticed changes in your appetite or weight, trouble concentrating, feelings of guilt or worthlessness, or any thoughts of not wanting to be alive during this time?

My concentration has gotten much worse. Spreadsheets that used to be second nature take me hours now—I lose the thread, reread the same assumptions over and over, and still worry I’ve missed something obvious before a presentation.
During these past three years, have you ever had thoughts of not wanting to be alive, or thoughts of hurting yourself?
I’m not sure what you mean by that. I’ve been feeling low, but I haven’t really thought about it in those terms.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight over these past few months?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear change in either one, at least not that I can point to.
Over these past few months, have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy, even after resting?
I’m not sure I’ve noticed a definite change in my energy, honestly.
Over these past three years, has there ever been a period of two weeks or more when your mood and other symptoms became noticeably worse or more intense than your usual baseline?
I don’t know. It’s hard for me to separate out whether there were specific stretches that were worse, versus just how I’ve generally been feeling.
Have there been any stretches during these three years when your mood felt a bit better, but you still had trouble falling asleep or staying asleep?

I can’t really think of a stretch where things felt better and my sleep was still bad. Lately I barely sleep in any useful way—I lie awake replaying client models, then wake up around three or four with my stomach tight. I go to work feeling like I never rested.
During this time, have you found yourself feeling unusually worthless, guilty, or overly critical of yourself?
Yes. If my manager questions one of my projections, I immediately take it as proof that I’m not as sharp as I used to be, that everyone can see I’m failing.
Have others noticed you moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or conversely, have you felt unusually restless or fidgety, during this time?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself being especially slow or fidgety, and nobody’s said anything to me about it.
Aside from feeling sad, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities or things you used to enjoy—like hobbies, time with family, or things outside of work?

Yes. I’ve stopped going to the volunteer teaching, yoga, and my book club—the things that used to keep my life outside work intact. And work is slipping too; I’ve had a formal performance warning because my models and presentations haven’t been up to standard.

Over these past three years, would you say that most of the time you've had several of these symptoms—like the sad mood, poor concentration, and guilt—happening together strongly enough to significantly disrupt your daily functioning, or has it felt more like a milder, low-grade heaviness that you've been able to push through most days?

It’s been more than just something I can push through. It’s really affected things—my work has slipped enough that I got a formal performance warning, and I’ve stopped going to the volunteer teaching, yoga, and book club. Those used to be the parts of my life that kept me going outside of work.

Have you ever had a period—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual but didn't feel tired, or found yourself talking more or taking risks you normally wouldn't?
I don’t think so. I can’t recall any stretch where I felt unusually energized or needed much less sleep without being tired, or acted out of character like that.

Going back to when this started three years ago, were your symptoms already this severe and impairing—affecting your work and causing you to pull back from activities—right from the beginning, or did it start out as a milder, low-grade sadness that has only recently become this intense?
It’s been going on for about three years, ever since the merger reorganized our Caribbean-market division.
